title: Feature Demo Clips Now Show the Real Product | vitalii.no
description:
My feature demo clips staged their UI beats as redrawn recreations of the real product — close, but not what a viewer would actually see on GitHub or on the site itself. Comparing a hand-drawn pilot against a version built from real recordings made it obvious which one was weaker, and every clip already made needed to be re-shot to match.

Every clip that needs a live UI beat now gets a shots/[id].json spec that both the recorder and the composition read. A script launches Playwright's Chromium and takes one screenshot per frame, computing scroll and mouse position from the frame number with keyframed interpolation — chosen over Playwright's own video capture because that timeline drifted about one-point-one times against wall-clock time on an earlier demo, walking the narration off the picture. The recorder now fails the whole run on purpose if any page request comes back at HTTP 400 or above, since a broken page recorded into a clip is worse than no clip at all. Two new primitives, LiveShot and LiveWindow, stage those frame dumps inside the Remotion composition, and the recording step runs on the GitHub Actions runner itself, right before render — nothing under public/rec is ever committed.

One screenshot per frame, locked to the voice-synced beat windows with zero timeline drift, replacing a webm capture that drifted roughly one-point-one times off the real clock.
